verses.119:2: Senhor, livrai a minha alma dos lábios iníquos, * e da língua enganadora.
verses.119:5: Ai de mim, {quia} {incolatus} se prolongou: † habitei com os {habitantibus} de Cedar: * {multum} foi forasteira a minha alma.
verses.119:7: Com os que {oderunt} a paz, eu era {pacificus}: * quando lhes falava, {impugnabant} sem motivo.

decisions.why: A verb in the Latin (the passive of tribuláre, 'when I was pressed / in distress'; Greek ἐν τῷ θλίβεσθαί με, an infinitive). The glossary's family is tribuláre → atribular, tribulátio → tribulação. Douay-Rheims and Matos Soares 1932 turn the verb into a noun ('In my trouble', 'Na minha tribulação'). The verse is the Gradual of Pent 2 and Lent II Friday.

options.label: quando estava atribulado
options.note: Draft. The verb stays a verb, in the glossary's family; 'atribulado' as an adjective is common speech even where the finite verb 'atribulam' was listed unknown by blind readers (glossary row tribuláre). The Latin's order (Ad Dóminum first) is kept for the head of the verse; the clause follows the verb, which is how Portuguese says it.

options.label: na minha tribulação
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and Douay-Rheims: a noun for the verb, shorter and familiar. A change of part of speech only, so D2 would allow it; kept as the option because the draft is just as sayable and keeps the Latin's clause.

decisions.why: exaudíre → escutar (D3). The subject (the Lord) is named by a pronoun, as 33:5 'e ele me escutou' and 3:5 do; the antiphon 'Clamávi, et exaudívit me' is cut from this verse and must read alone.

options.label: me escutou
options.note: v2, from the stylist: the subject is left unnamed as in the Latin (et exaudívit me), and the 'e ele' hiatus at the close of a short colon goes. Grammar only (D2). 'Ao Senhor' at the head of the verse names who heard.

options.label: ele me escutou
options.note: Draft 1: 33:5's build, and word for word the Brazilian Liturgia das Horas (CNBB) line of this psalm (fetched, ps119/circulation.md; circulation, not sense).

options.label: escutou-me
options.note: 21:25b's build (enclisis); no pronoun.

decisions.latin: Quid detur tibi, aut quid apponátur tibi
decisions.why: Two present subjunctives (Greek optatives, δοθείη … προστεθείη) in a deliberative question. Portuguese asks this with the future. The singular 'tibi' is not God (whom this psalter calls vós), so it is 'te' (rule 3): who is meant — the psalmist, or the deceitful tongue itself — the Latin leaves open and so does 'te'. The repetition of 'quid … tibi' is kept.

options.label: Que te será dado, ou que te será acrescentado

forms.detur: Que te será dado, ou que te será acrescentado

options.note: Draft; Matos Soares 1932 has the first half word for word. +3 syllables on the Latin colon, accepted: shortening it would drop one of the two 'te'.

options.label: Que se te dará, ou que se te acrescentará

forms.detur: Que se te dará, ou que se te acrescentará

options.note: Shorter, but 'se te' twice is bookish and 'dará … acrescentará' chimes.

decisions.why: The crux of the psalm. 'ad' + accusative (Greek πρὸς γλῶσσαν δολίαν) can be 'for', 'towards', 'against' or 'in answer to'. Read as said to the tongue, it asks what the tongue will get; read as said to the psalmist, it asks what remedy he will be given against it — and 119:4 then answers: the sharp arrows of the mighty. The Latin does not choose. Matos Soares 1932 makes it a vocative ('ó língua enganadora'), which is the Hebrew's construction, not the Latin's preposition. The v1 ambiguity reader heard 'te' as possibly God, after 'Senhor … livrai' (vós) in 119:2, and found 'para' unclear; the stylist asked for 'à'.

options.label: para
options.note: Draft. 'para a língua enganadora' keeps both readings open: what is given 'for' the tongue — as its due, or as the answer to it.

options.label: contra
options.note: Decides for the reading in which a weapon or remedy is given against the tongue; clearer, and it makes 119:4 an answer. Refused as option 0 because it closes what the Latin leaves open (D2).

options.label: à
options.note: The stylist's proposal (DRB 'to a deceitful tongue'): smoother, no 'para a' hiatus. Refused as option 0: set after 'te', 'à língua' is heard as apposition — 'to you, the tongue' — which leans to the vocative reading (the Hebrew's) and closes the question the Latin leaves open.

options.label: ó (vocative)
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 'ó língua enganadora': the Hebrew's address to the tongue. The Latin has a preposition, not a vocative; refused. (The verse would read '… acrescentado, * ó língua enganadora?')

decisions.why: A substantive, 'of the mighty one' (τοῦ δυνατοῦ; DRB 'of the mighty'). potens → poderoso at 23:8, 51:3, 88:9; 77:65 made it 'um valente' where the context is a warrior drunk with wine. 126:4 'Sicut sagíttæ in manu poténtis' has the same phrase and should copy this one.

options.label: poderoso
options.note: Draft, with Matos Soares 1932 ('Setas agudas do poderoso'). Leaves open who the mighty one is — God or a warrior — as the Latin does.

options.label: valente
options.note: 77:65's word; makes him a fighting man, which narrows.

options.label: guerreiro
options.note: Diurnal Monástico 1962 ('do guerreiro'), from the Hebrew gibbor; says more than potens. Refused.

decisions.why: The glossary row carbónes → carvões (17:9, 17:13 = 17:14, and this verse listed; 139:11 to come). The stylist heard 'carvões' as grill charcoal, cold and black, and asked for 'brasas'.

options.label: carvões
options.note: Kept: the glossary row, so the psalter says one word for carbónes; 'devastadores' after it says they burn. Changing it here would split the row or reopen Ps 17.

options.label: brasas
options.note: The stylist's: the live coal, concrete; the row's own named option (DM1962's word). If taken, it should be taken for the whole row.

decisions.why: desolatórius is a church-Latin coinage, 'that makes desolate' (Lewis & Short, citing this verse); DRB 'coals that lay waste'. The Greek ἐρημικοῖς is 'of the desert' — the Latin read it actively, and we follow the Latin (rule 1). carbónes → carvões (glossary row). The cognate 'desolar/desolador' is heard in Brazil as 'saddening' (glossary row desoláre, 78:7).

options.label: devastadores
options.note: Draft. 'That lay waste', DRB's sense, in a plain word; keeps the active force of -tórius.

options.label: desoladores
options.note: The cognate, exact in the dictionary; but 'uma cena desoladora' is a sad scene, and the ear takes that first.

options.label: devoradores
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: an image the Latin does not have (devouring). Refused.

options.label: do deserto
options.note: The Greek's sense (ἐρημικοῖς), which the Latin does not follow. Refused under rule 1.

decisions.why: After 'Ai de mim' Portuguese can give the cause with 'que' or 'porque'. The stylist heard the causal 'que' as slightly archaic and open to being taken as a relative.

options.label: porque
options.note: v2, from the stylist: the plain causal, and quia's usual word in this psalter. One syllable more. His other changes (dropping the article of 'a minha', the verb before the subject) refused: rule 5 keeps the article before possessives.

options.label: que
options.note: Draft 1: shorter, idiomatic after 'Ai de mim'.

decisions.why: incolátus is sojourning as an alien (παροικία); the same verse closes 'íncola fuit' (παρῴκησεν), an echo in both Latin and Greek. íncola → forasteiro is settled (D39), but Portuguese has no noun of 'forasteiro'. 118:54 'in loco peregrinatiónis meæ' (the same Greek noun, παροικία) is 'no lugar da minha peregrinação'. The Office of the Dead sings this colon as its Vespers antiphon ('Heu mihi Dómine, quia incolátus meus prolongátus est').

options.label: a minha peregrinação
options.note: Draft. By D15's Greek test it shares 118:54's word (both παροικία); 'peregrinação' is the Christian word for life as a sojourn and needs no footnote. Cost: the echo with 'forasteira' at the end of the verse is heard only in sense, not in sound. The v1 ambiguity reader heard 'a religious pilgrimage' first; kept — life as a sojourn is exactly what the Church hears in this colon (it is the Vespers antiphon of the Office of the Dead), and the verse goes on to name the foreign tents. If the exile sense must be heard first, option 1 does it.

options.label: o meu tempo de forasteiro
options.note: Keeps the echo incolátus / íncola as forasteiro / forasteira; supplies 'tempo', and is two syllables longer.

options.label: o meu desterro
options.note: Matos Soares 1932. Desterro is banishment, a sharper sense than sojourning; refused.

decisions.why: The Latin repeats the root (verb and participle); the Greek does too (κατεσκήνωσα … σκηνωμάτων, though of tents). Matos Soares 1932 varies it ('habitei com os moradores').

options.label: habitantes
options.note: Draft. The repetition is the Latin's (D2).

options.label: moradores
options.note: Matos Soares 1932; avoids the jingle, drops the repetition.

decisions.why: multum here is adverbial, 'much / long' (πολλὰ; DRB 'my soul hath been long a sojourner'; Matos Soares 1932 'Muito tempo andou peregrinando'). Bare 'Muito foi forasteira' is heard as degree ('very much a stranger'), not length.

options.label: muito tempo
options.note: Draft. The duration DRB and Matos Soares both hear; after 'se prolongou' in the first colon, time is plainly the sense. Same syllable count as the Latin colon.

options.label: muito
options.note: The Latin's one word, leaving degree or length open; heard as degree first. The v1 Latinist's fix (minor): 'tempo' narrows multum to duration. Refused: bare 'muito' is heard as degree ('very much a stranger'), which is a narrowing too, and the wrong one after 'se prolongou'; the Latinist himself calls duration the likely sense and 'tempo' defensible.

decisions.why: odérunt is a perfect with present sense (glossary row odísse); set beside 'eram' the Portuguese needs the past for sequence. Greek present participle μισούντων.

options.label: odiavam
options.note: Draft, with Matos Soares 1932: tense follows 'eu era'. The Holy Thursday antiphon cut from this verse reads alone as a narrative.

options.label: odeiam
options.note: The present sense of odísse, as 24:19 and 25:5 have it; jars against 'eu era'. The v2 Latinist (minor) asked for it: the preteritive perfect keeps the enemies' abiding character.

decisions.why: The Latin echoes pacem / pacíficus. The glossary row pacíficus (36:37) chose 'de paz' because the cognate is a proparoxytone at a cadence; here it stands before the asterisk. It said 119:7 would decide its own build.

options.label: de paz
options.note: Draft. 'eu era de paz' keeps the echo with 'a paz' as the Latin keeps it, ends the colon on a stressed syllable, and follows 36:37 ('o homem de paz'). Risk: a slight jingle.

options.label: pacífico
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 ('eu era pacífico'); DRB 'peaceable'. The cognate; proparoxytone before the mark.

decisions.why: impugnáre → combater at 34:1 ('combatei os que me combatem'); the Greek here is ἐπολέμουν, 'made war on me'. gratis → sem motivo (glossary row; 119:7 is listed there). Matos Soares 1932 has 'contradiziam-me', which narrows to words.

options.label: combatiam
options.note: 34:1's verb, the image of fighting kept. v2: the subject pronoun supplied (the stylist), so the clause does not open on a clitic after the comma; grammar only (D2). Cost: the colon grows to +5 by the heuristic.

options.label: me combatiam
options.note: Draft 1: shorter; proclisis after a comma, which the stylist heard as everyday speech.

options.label: contradiziam
options.note: Matos Soares 1932. Reduces the war to argument; refused.

choices.119:1: Titulus: the Latin (DO) has no 'Canticum graduum' line (D7; collation/report.md lists tituli as omitted), and Ps 133 — also a Gradual Psalm — carries none; so Ps 119 has none, and Pss 120–133 should have none. For the day tituli are added, the formula is proposed in glossary.md (Formulas) as 'Cântico dos degraus' (open). The verse opens on 'Ao Senhor', as the Latin opens on 'Ad Dóminum'. The Brazilian Liturgia das Horas (CNBB) has 'e ele me escutou' here — fetched, ps119/circulation.md; it is a Hebrew-family text and counted only as circulation, not sense. v1 ambiguity reader listed 'atribulado' as unknown; kept (the glossary's family; 'na minha tribulação' is option 1 of tribularer).
choices.119:2: líbera → livrar (glossary). lábia iníqua → 'lábios iníquos' (iníquos is paroxytone: i-NÍ-quos). lingua dolósa → 'língua enganadora', as 108:3 and the dolósus row (which lists 119:2–3); the same two words are in the CNBB Liturgia das Horas line of this psalm (circulation only). v1 ambiguity reader listed 'iníquos' as unknown and heard 'a minha alma' as the spiritual soul first; both kept — glossary rows iníquus and ánima mea, which note the same cost.
choices.119:3: The repeated 'língua enganadora' of 119:2–3 repeats as the Latin's does.
choices.119:4: Verbless, as the Latin: the line stands as an answer to 119:3. 'Setas agudas' is 44:6's build (acútus of a point → agudo, D44 row novácula). No article, as Matos Soares 1932.
choices.119:5: DO's inline (6) is not reproduced. Cedar kept as the name (Qedar), no gloss. 'Ai de mim, que …' renders 'Heu mihi, quia': the exclamative 'que' is the natural Portuguese causal after 'Ai de mim' (grammar, D2). 'Cedar' was listed as unknown by the v1 ambiguity reader; a proper name, kept without gloss.
choices.119:7: The Latin's 'Cum his, qui' is 'with these, who'; 'Com os que' is the Portuguese form (grammar). No subject supplied for 'impugnábant' — 'os que odiavam a paz' is the only candidate.

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from parallels (Latin, LXX, Hebrew, DRB, MS1932, DM1962; DO pt-PT not used as evidence). Glossary applied: escutar (D3), livrar, forasteiro (D39), carvões, setas, língua enganadora, sem motivo, combater (34:1), de paz (36:37), peregrinação (118:54, same Greek). Hard readings: 119:3 'ad linguam dolósam' (kept open with 'para'), 119:4 desolatóriis (the Latin's active sense, not the Greek's 'of the desert'), 119:5 incolátus. Liturgical use checked by grep in DO (Graduals Pent02-0 and Quad2-5; antiphons; Office of the Dead; Holy Thursday) and Brazilian circulation by fetch (CNBB Liturgia das Horas, Ave Maria, Pe. Ney Brasil) — ps119/circulation.md. Titulus: none, matching Ps 133 and D7; formula proposed in the glossary.

Hard checks pass. Soft: 119:1 first colon +5 by the heuristic (about +2 in the mouth: 'quando‿estava‿atribulado' elides twice) — accepted to keep the verb; 'na minha tribulação' (option 1) is the right length if the ear wants it. 119:3 both cola +3 (two 'te' kept; 'para a' elides). 119:5c and 119:7b +3, accepted (supplied 'tempo'; 'me combatiam'). 119:2/119:3 finals rhyme on 'enganadora': the Latin has the same echo (dolósa / dolósam), so it stays.
One minor; refused, with the Latinist's own concession that it is defensible. Overall: faithful; marks match.

outcomes.remark: multum: 'tempo' narrows to duration; fix 'muito foi forasteira'
outcomes.reason: bare 'muito' is heard as degree, a wrong narrowing after 'se prolongou'; duration is what DRB and MS1932 hear and what the Latinist calls likely.

audit.note: 5 remarks; 3 taken (119:1 'e me escutou', 119:5 'porque', 119:7 'eles me combatiam'), 2 kept as options (119:3 'à', 119:4 'brasas'). Best line 119:2; worst 119:7.

outcomes.remark: 'e ele' hiatus, pronoun conversational; 'e me escutou'
'para a' hiatus and unclear; 'à língua enganadora'
outcomes.reason: after 'te', 'à língua' is heard as apposition (you, the tongue), leaning to the vocative reading and closing the Latin's open 'ad'.
glossary row carbónes → carvões (Ps 17); a change should be made for the whole row, and 'devastadores' already says they burn.

outcomes.remark: causal 'que' archaic; 'porque se prolongou minha peregrinação'
outcomes.reason: 'porque' taken; dropping the article before the possessive and moving the verb refused (rule 5; order change gains nothing once 'porque' is in).

outcomes.remark: clause opening on a clitic; 'eles me combatiam'

audit.note: 9 ambiguities, 3 unknown words (Cedar, iníquos, atribulado). None changed the text; the one real risk is 119:3 'te' heard as God.

outcomes.reason: the Latin's word; glossary row ánima mea.

outcomes.remark: 'te' may be heard as God after 'Senhor … livrai'
outcomes.reason: God is vós throughout, so 'te' marks a change of addressee, as tibi does; naming the addressee would decide the crux (tongue or psalmist) the Latin leaves open. Recorded in decision adlinguam.

outcomes.remark: 'para' does not signal who receives what
outcomes.reason: the unclearness is the Latin's 'ad'; 'contra' and 'ó' are there as the two ways of closing it.

outcomes.remark: verbless line floats, not linked to v. 3
outcomes.reason: verbless in the Latin; supplying a verb would decide how it answers v. 3.
the Latin's openness, kept on purpose (decision potentis).
the Latin's image; 'brasas' is the option.
life as sojourn is the sense the Church prays here (Office of the Dead antiphon); 'o meu tempo de forasteiro' is the option for the exile sense.

outcomes.remark: 'forasteira a minha alma': spiritual or self
'eu era de paz': peaceable or at peace
outcomes.reason: heard as 'a man of peace', the right sense.

audit.note: v2: 119:1 'e me escutou'; 119:5 'porque'; 119:7 'eles me combatiam' (all stylist, grammar only). New decisions carbonibus (brasas option) and quia; 'à' added to adlinguam. Draft 1 kept as prayed.v1.json.
v2: hard pass. New soft flag 119:7b +5 (the supplied eles), accepted for the stylist's reason; the others as in v1.
Gate clean of majors: one minor, held as an option. Overall: faithful, Septuagintal readings kept, marks match.

outcomes.reason: beside eu era / falava Portuguese needs the past for sequence (the Latinist calls it defensible); odeiam against eu era jars in the ear; MS1932 odiavam.
